what: Police stop Tommy Robinson on his way back to London from Russian trip

clean_source_blocks.text: Met seizes far-right activist’s phones after he disembarks flight at Heathrow under counter-terrorism provisions British police say they stopped the far-right activist Tommy Robinson and seized his phones as he returned from a trip to Russia. Robinson, whose real name is Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, met Elon Musk’s father in Moscow during his trip. Continue reading...

Met seizes far-right activist’s phones after he disembarks flight at Heathrow under counter-terrorism provisions British police say they stopped the far-right activist Tommy Robinson and seized his phones as he returned from a trip to Russia. Robinson, whose real name is Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, met Elon Musk’s father in Moscow during his trip. Russia is regarded by the UK and most western powers as a hostile state, with defence officials fearing that Vladimir Putin’s regime may stage an attack as early as 2030. The Metropolitan police said Robinson had been stopped after getting off a flight at Heathrow airport in London from Russia via Turkey. His phones were seized under legislation designed to stop potential threats to the UK and the Guardian understands those devices will be sent for examination.

While he was in Russia, social media accounts linked to Robinson called for protests after last Monday’s knife attack in Belfast. The monitoring group Hope Not Hate says Robinson, 43, is the “best-known far-right extremist in Britain”. A Met spokesperson said: “Officers stopped a man in his 40s at Heathrow airport at around 17.00 on Saturday 13 June, following his return to the UK from Russia via Turkey. “He was stopped under the provisions of Schedule 3 of the Counter-Terrorism and Border Security Act 2019. The man was interviewed by officers and his communication devices were seized. He was subsequently released.”

“It is immaterial whether a person is aware that activity in which they are or have been engaged is hostile activity, or whether a state for or on behalf of which, or in the interests of which, a hostile act is carried out has instigated, sanctioned, or is otherwise aware of, the carrying out of the act.” On social media, Robinson portrayed himself as the victim of an overbearing state persecuting him for his political beliefs. He said he was held for about three hours, with two phones seized. He said he would need money for legal costs and asked supporters for donations.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: The Guardian World]
Met seizes far-right activist’s phones after he disembarks flight at Heathrow under counter-terrorism provisions

British police say they stopped the far-right activist Tommy Robinson and seized his phones as he returned from a trip to Russia.

Robinson, whose real name is Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, met Elon Musk’s father in Moscow during his trip.

Russia is regarded by the UK and most western powers as a hostile state, with defence officials fearing that Vladimir Putin’s regime may stage an attack as early as 2030.

The Metropolitan police said Robinson had been stopped after getting off a flight at Heathrow airport in London from Russia via Turkey.

His phones were seized under legislation designed to stop potential threats to the UK and the Guardian understands those devices will be sent for examination.

While he was in Russia, social media accounts linked to Robinson called for protests after last Monday’s knife attack in Belfast.

The monitoring group Hope Not Hate says Robinson, 43, is the “best-known far-right extremist in Britain”.

A Met spokesperson said: “Officers stopped a man in his 40s at Heathrow airport at around 17.00 on Saturday 13 June, following his return to the UK from Russia via Turkey.

“He was stopped under the provisions of Schedule 3 of the Counter-Terrorism and Border Security Act 2019. The man was interviewed by officers and his communication devices were seized. He was subsequently released.”

A Home Office code of practice for schedule 3 of the Counter-Terrorism and Border Security Act 2019 explains it can be used by police against a person suspected of being “engaged in hostile activity … if the person is or has been concerned in the commission, preparation or instigation of a hostile act that is or may be (a) carried out for, or on behalf of, a state other than the United Kingdom, or (b) otherwise in the interests of a state other than the United Kingdom.

“It is immaterial whether a person is aware that activity in which they are or have been engaged is hostile activity, or whether a state for or on behalf of which, or in the interests of which, a hostile act is carried out has instigated, sanctioned, or is otherwise aware of, the carrying out of the act.”

On social media, Robinson portrayed himself as the victim of an overbearing state persecuting him for his political beliefs. He said he was held for about three hours, with two phones seized. He said he would need money for legal costs and asked supporters for donations.

payload.title: Poliisi pysäytti Tommy Robinsonin Heathrow’lla Venäjän-matkan jälkeen
payload.summary: Britannian poliisi pysäytti äärioikeistoaktivisti Tommy Robinsonin Lontoon Heathrow’n lentoasemalla hänen palattuaan Venäjältä Turkin kautta. Poliisin mukaan Robinsonia kuulusteltiin ja hänen viestintälaitteitaan takavarikoitiin terrorisminvastaisen rajaturvallisuuslain nojalla.
payload.content:
Britannian poliisi pysäytti äärioikeistoaktivisti Tommy Robinsonin Lontoon Heathrow’n lentoasemalla lauantaina 13. kesäkuuta, kun hän oli palannut maahan Venäjältä Turkin kautta. Metropolitan Police kertoi kuulustelleensa häntä ja takavarikoineensa hänen viestintälaitteitaan Counter-Terrorism and Border Security Act 2019 -lain Schedule 3 -säännösten nojalla.

## Pysäytys tapahtui Heathrow’lla

Poliisin mukaan noin nelikymppinen mies pysäytettiin Heathrow’lla noin kello 17 paikallista aikaa. Hänet kuulusteltiin, hänen viestintälaitteensa otettiin haltuun ja hänet vapautettiin myöhemmin. Guardianin tietojen mukaan takavarikoidut laitteet on tarkoitus lähettää tutkittaviksi.

Robinson, oikealta nimeltään Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, oli ollut Venäjällä, missä hän tapasi Elon Muskin isän. Venäjää pidetään Britanniassa ja useimmissa länsimaissa vihamielisenä valtiona. Britannian puolustusviranomaiset ovat lähdeaineiston mukaan varoittaneet mahdollisuudesta, että Vladimir Putinin hallinto voisi toteuttaa hyökkäyksen jo vuonna 2030.

Kyseessä oleva lainsäädäntö on tarkoitettu mahdollisten Britanniaan kohdistuvien uhkien torjumiseen rajalla. Poliisin siteeraaman lainkohdan mukaan henkilön tietoisuus mahdollisesta vihamielisestä toiminnasta ei ole ratkaisevaa arvioitaessa, voidaanko säännöksiä soveltaa. Sama koskee sitä, onko vieras valtio tietoinen teosta tai hyväksynyt sen.

## Robinson reagoi sosiaalisessa mediassa

Robinson kuvasi sosiaalisessa mediassa joutuneensa valtion liiallisen vallankäytön kohteeksi poliittisten näkemystensä vuoksi. Hänen mukaansa häntä pidettiin kiinni noin kolme tuntia ja häneltä takavarikoitiin kaksi puhelinta. Hän kertoi tarvitsevansa rahaa oikeudenkäyntikuluihin ja pyysi tukijoiltaan lahjoituksia.

Robinsoniin liitetyt sosiaalisen median tilit olivat hänen Venäjän-matkansa aikana kehottaneet ihmisiä protesteihin Belfastissa tapahtuneen puukotuksen jälkeen. Seurantaryhmä Hope Not Hate on kuvannut 43-vuotiasta Robinsonia Britannian tunnetuimmaksi äärioikeistolaiseksi ekstremistiksi.
summary_bullets: Metropolitan Police pysäytti Tommy Robinsonin Heathrow’lla hänen palattuaan Venäjältä Turkin kautta.
Poliisi takavarikoi hänen viestintälaitteitaan terrorisminvastaisen rajaturvallisuuslain nojalla.
Robinson sanoi sosiaalisessa mediassa olleensa kiinni noin kolme tuntia ja pyysi tukijoiltaan rahaa oikeuskuluihin.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu paketin tietoihin Metropolitan Policen toimista, Robinsonin omiin sosiaalisen median väitteisiin ja taustatietoihin hänen Venäjän-matkastaan. Väitteitä ei laajennettu lähdeaineiston ulkopuolelle.
